grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Chinese has no he/she difference in speech: tā sounds the same. The plural ending 们 (men) makes a group of people.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Nouns do not change for plural. Use a number and a measure word, or just the context.

grammar.title: 是: to be
text: Use 是 (shì) between two nouns: A 是 B. Do not use 是 before an adjective.

grammar.title: Verbs do not change
text: Chinese verbs never change their form. Time words or small particles show the time.
ex: tomorrow I will go to Beijing
we watch TV in the evening

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Word order is Subject, Verb, Object, like English. Time and place come before the verb.

grammar.title: Negation
text: Use 不 (bù) before most verbs and adjectives. Use 没 (méi) for 有 and for the past. Say 不 as bú before a fourth tone.
rows: 我 不 喝 茶
ex: I do not have a car
I do not want to go
tā méi gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Add 吗 (ma) to the end of a statement to make a yes-no question. Or use the verb pattern: verb + 不 + verb.
rows: 你 是 学生 吗
你 去 不 去

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stay in the same place as the answer. You do not move them to the front.

grammar.title: Particles
text: Small words at the end or after a word give the grammar. They have no meaning of their own.
ex: wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū

grammar.title: This, that, which
text: Put a measure word after 这, 那 and 哪 when you point at a thing: 这个, 那个, 哪个.
ex: zhè běn shū shì wǒ de
nà gè rén shì wǒ de lǎoshī

grammar.title: Adjectives
text: Adjectives work like verbs. Do not use 是. Put 很 (very) in front, even when you only mean "is".

grammar.title: Wanting and asking
text: 想 means "would like to" and 要 means "want to, will". For polite asking, begin with 请 or 请问.
ex: I would like to go to China
excuse me, where is the toilet?

grammar.title: Existing and having
text: 有 means "have" and also "there is". 没有 is the opposite. 在 tells you where something is.
rows: 桌子 上 有 书
书 在 桌子 上
ex: I do not have a brother

grammar.title: Measure words
text: Between a number and a noun you need a measure word. 个 (ge) works for most things.

grammar.title: Formal and informal
text: Use 您 (nín) for one older or respected person. Use 你 with friends. 请 makes any request polite.

grammar.title: Commands
text: A command is just the verb. Use 请 to be polite and 别 or 不要 to say "do not".

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: These helper verbs go before the main verb. 会 is "can" by learning, 能 is "can" by ability or chance, 可以 is "may".

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: 在 (zài) is "at, in, on". Use place words like 上 (on), 里 (in), 下 (under) after the noun.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the chair
the school is next to the park

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Use 比 (bǐ) to compare: A 比 B + adjective. Use 最 (zuì) for "the most".
rows: 他 比 我 高
我 没有 他 高
ex: this one is cheaper than that one
I am not as tall as him

grammar.title: Past, now and future
text: Add 了 for a finished action, 过 for "have ever", 在 for "is doing", and 会 or 要 for the future.
ex: the train is about to leave

grammar.title: Everyday sentences
text: Short sentences you can use every day.
ex: I go to work by bus
I watch TV in the evening
I go to bed at eleven

sounds.intro: Chinese is written in pinyin, the Latin spelling of the sounds, with four tones. The tone changes the meaning, so learn it with every word.
rows: high and flat, like holding a note
like the p, t, k in "spin": no puff of air
bā 八, dà 大, gē 歌
like English p, t, k with a strong puff of air
pà 怕, tā 他, kě 渴
like English (h is a little rougher)
mā 妈, nǐ 你, fā 发, lái 来, hǎo 好
like "j" in "jeep", with the tongue flat and the lips smiling
like "ch" in "cheese", with a puff of air, lips smiling
like "j" in "jam", with the tongue curled back
like "ch" in "church", tongue curled back, with a puff
like English y and w (they are spellings of i and u)
ee, like "see"; after z, c, s, zh, ch, sh, r it is a short buzz
nǐ 你, sì 四, shí 十
say "ee" with rounded lips, like French "u"
huì 会, liù 六, wèn 问
notes: Do not read pinyin like English: q is not "kw", x is not "ks", c is "ts" and zh is like "j".
When a 3rd tone comes before another 3rd tone, the first one is said as a 2nd tone: nǐ hǎo is said "ní hǎo". The spelling stays the same.
不 (bù) changes to bú before a 4th tone: bú shì. 一 (yī) is said yí before a 4th tone and yì before the others.
In pinyin, words are written together, and names start with a capital letter.
